items.title: Mozambique: Government plans to track and monitor businesses on digital platforms
items.summary: The intention was announced today in Maputo by the spokesperson for the Council of Ministers, Inocêncio Impissa, on the sidelines of the body’s 30th ordinary session, in response to questions about the growth of digital platforms providing credit and other economic activities carried out in the virtual space According to the official, the measure falls within the implementation of the recently approved decree on electronic transactions and digital commerce, as well as new mechanisms for monitoring activities carried out online “Recently, a decree was approved on electronic transactions involving various types of businesses and electronic commerce,” he said The spokesperson added that the new legislation should ensure “the compliance of these activities”, “the formalisation of these activities” and define how they participate “in the process of collectively building Mozambique” According to Impissa, entities such as the Digital Transformation Agency will be responsible for monitoring operators that conduct economic activities through digital platforms The official said that the…

items.title: Mozambique: Government advocates mobilising sustainable financing to boost development
items.summary: The Secretary of State for Treasury and Budget, Amílcar Tivane, stressed the need to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation, improve public expenditure efficiency and attract responsible private investment as essential measures to drive Mozambique’s economic development In his address at the report launch on Friday, 16 October 2026, Tivane highlighted the longstanding partnership between Mozambique and the AfDB, established in 1977, which has resulted in the financing of major development projects and the production of technical knowledge to support public policy formulation The Secretary of State noted that economic growth slowed from 2.1% in 2024 to 0.2% in 2025. Amílcar Tivane explained that this slowdown reflects the effects of post-election disruptions, climate shocks, financing constraints and the weak performance of important sectors of the economy.

items.title: New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
items.summary: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security The EU on Tuesday presented a new Arctic Strategy that outlines the bloc's priorities in the key region amid challenges such as security threats, climate change and mining Russia is building up its military power in the Arctic, and US President Donald Trump has threatened Greenland , saying the Danish territory is needed for American security interests but later signed a deal with Denmark over US military access to the territory . China is also investing in the region and has shipping ambitions there The northern parts of Finland and Sweden, along with Greenland are located within the Arctic, meaning part of the region is in the European neighborhood.

items.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
items.summary: Ameth Bek Hospital in Abyei town has been treating people wounded in Monday's attack on the market Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 300 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 153 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011 South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest.

items.title: Residents warned not to drink tap water after hundreds fall sick near South Africa capital
items.summary: Tests found traces of E. coli in water supplied to residents living near Pretoria Residents living near South Africa's capital, Pretoria, have been warned not to drink or cook with tap water after more than 400 people, mostly children under four, fell ill after drinking contaminated water The cases were detected in Tshwane, the area which includes Pretoria, after people reported to their local hospital with "stomach cramps and diarrhoea" over a two-week period, officials said No deaths have been reported but high levels of E. coli were found in the water Tshwane has faced numerous outbreaks from waterborne diseases in recent years. In 2023, 29 people were killed by a cholera outbreak in a township just outside Pretoria That outbreak, in Hammanskraal, was linked to substandard water purification practices In 2025, officials confirmed 48 cases of typhoid in the same area east of Pretoria.

items.title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?
items.summary: President Donald Trump has been boasting about the performance of the US economy ahead of the midterm congressional elections, claiming he has boosted incomes, reduced inflation and created jobs Trump has repeatedly said: "We have the hottest country anywhere in the world." While the overall US economy is faring better than many expected after Trump launched his sweeping "Liberation Day" tariffs in 2025, there's evidence those import taxes and the impact of the US-Israel war with Iran have pushed up inflation, with the harmful effects felt by most American households The US economy is also being helped by an AI investment boom, and could falter if that spending were to dry up So how does all this feel for the average American?

items.title: Lawyers must practice their profession free from threats
items.summary: Maputo, 20 Oct (AIM) – The chairwoman of the Mozambican Bar Association, Thera Dai, said on Monday that every single lawyer must be able to practice their profession free from threats , in an environment of freedom and independence Thera Dai was speaking to reporters in Maputo following a march by lawyers in memory of Elvino Dias, who was murdered on October 19, 2024. Dias was the lawyer and legal advisor of the presidential candidate Venâncio Mondlane, backed by the Optimistic Party for the Development of Mozambique (Podemos), in the general elections held on 9 October. Dias and Paulo Guambe, a Podemos election agent, were shot dead by unknown assailants in central Maputo on 19 October. Dias was murdered when he was preparing a challenge to be submitted to the Constitutional Council, Mozambique’s highest body in matters of electoral law, in order to denounce the alleged irregularities that occurred during the elections. “In paying this tribute, we reaffirm that no lawyer should be intimidated, threatened, or placed at risk for the legitimate practice of their profession.

items.title: France plans 'massive' weekend police surge amid protests
items.summary: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu told parliament the government would respond and reinforce police in major cities. He also accused extreme-left groups of trying to hijack what began as protests. DW has more Follow below for the latest on the protests and unrest in France and other parts of Europe on Tuesday, October 20: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said 500 troops would be sent to the city of Milan until January. They will help police after violent clashes in the city over the weekend Meloni said a Cabinet meeting also approved measures to make the detention of minors easier, to impose fines on their parents for any damage and to introduce the crime of "violent participation in a demonstration." "Protesting is a right, devastating our cities is not," Meloni said in a video on X At least four other cities — Lyon, Bordeaux, Nice and Marseille — have announced continued localized restrictions that will take effect on Tuesday night In Lyon, the prefect of the Rhone region, ordered another curfew from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m.
